assessment.nobel_worthiness: Clear physiological discovery (incretin action of GLP-1, its processing and degradation) translated into therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are all exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic action, GLP-2) and Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) are the clearest basic-science contributors; Knudsen led the pharmacological engineering of long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's early sequence and peptide work is a real contribution whose weighting is disputed, and other key investigators outside the supplied credit may matter.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and very large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, and omitted contributors, is unresolved; the three-person limit forces exclusion of a credited contributor.
Whether the committee prefers a physiology-centred or a drug-development-centred award; I have not independently verified priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and experimental physiology a method for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity in intact circuits, and is used across behaviour, circuit mapping and early therapeutic efforts such as vision restoration. It is a tool, but one with exceptional originality and breadth of enabling impact.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Bamberg contributed to its biophysics and early expression; Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenböck made the neuronal application and demonstrations. Credit is a genuine multi-party dispute; a configuration of Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth spans channel discovery and neural use, but excludes Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck.
assessment.maturity: Established for over a decade with massive independent adoption; timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is contested and the three-laureate limit leaves out major contributors.
Clinical translation is still early; the case rests on method impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered chimeric antigen receptor T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapeutics; the concept, design and clinical proof are clear and highly consequential.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulated CARs), June (clinical development of CD19 CAR-T) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials) cover concept, translation and the adoptive-therapy lineage. Earlier receptor-chimera work by others (for example Eshhar, Kuwana) is outside the supplied names and I cannot resolve its weight.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long-term follow-up; timely, though long-term safety and solid-tumour efficacy are still evolving.
uncertainties: Earlier inventors of chimeric receptors are not in the credit list, complicating fair attribution.
Limited effect so far in solid tumours and secondary-malignancy and toxicity questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic dissection of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to an antisense oligonucleotide (nusinersen) that changed the natural history of a fatal childhood neurodegenerative disease. It is a rare case of tight mechanism-to-cure logic and established proof for splice-switching therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer supplied the splicing-regulatory insight and target-site logic and Bennett the antisense chemistry and drug development, with a natural two-person configuration. Contributions of the original SMN gene discoverers (Melki, Lefebvre) and of Adrian Krainer's and Ionis collaborators are outside this entry's credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term patient data; recognition is plausible now, though broader antisense field credit remains evolving.
uncertainties: Gene discovery of SMN1/SMN2 is a separate part of the story and may need separate recognition.
Interaction with the wider oligonucleotide field and other SMA therapies (gene therapy, risdiplam).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunotherapy. The discovery is clear and conceptually unifying.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified the cGAS enzyme and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. Ishikawa co-discovered STING; Sun and Wu were key coauthors in Chen's laboratory and are unlikely laureates under a conventional design. Credit is plausible for two people, but the STING priority question has some ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: Over a decade of independent confirmation; therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) is not yet successful, so recognition would rest on mechanism.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit is not yet demonstrated; the case is mainly mechanistic.
Split of credit between STING and cGAS and the roles of trainees and co-discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identification linked a hypothalamic neuropeptide system to arousal stability and showed that narcolepsy type 1 arises from loss of these neurons, with orexin-receptor antagonists now in clinical use for insomnia. A clean bridge from molecular neuroscience to a human disease mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexin and its receptors and the narcolepsy phenotype in knockout mice; de Lecea and Kilduff independently described hypocretin transcripts; Mignot identified the canine and human receptor/peptide defect. Priority between orexin and hypocretin groups is the main attribution tension; the proposed three emphasise peptide discovery and the narcolepsy link.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed for two decades with approved drugs; timely.
uncertainties: Parallel discovery by two groups and a five-person credit list make a three-laureate allocation contentious.
Autoimmune basis of orexin neuron loss in human narcolepsy is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing), established a core principle of proteostasis with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central figures; Walter's laboratory defined Ire1 signalling and mRNA splicing, and Mori's identified the UPR element and the transcriptional arm. Other contributors (for example Kaufman, Ron, Schekman-related ER work) are not in the supplied credit and could affect fairness.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively replicated; recognised by earlier major prizes, so a Nobel would be timely but not urgent.
uncertainties: Direct therapeutic consequences remain limited, so the claim is basic-mechanistic.
Overlap with other ER stress investigators outside the credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signalling established a central controller of growth, metabolism and nutrient sensing, with consequences for cancer, immune suppression, ageing and metabolic disease, including clinical rapalog use.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and is the pivotal discoverer; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and the target is foundational chemical biology; Sabatini defined mammalian mTORC1/2 and nutrient sensing. Contributions of the Sabatini-era community and rapamycin's original discoverers (Vezina, Sehgal) complicate credit, and Sabatini's recent professional controversy may affect committee deliberation, which I treat as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across systems with approved therapeutics; timely.
uncertainties: A single-discoverer emphasis on Hall versus a three-person configuration is unresolved.
Non-scientific considerations around one credited person and credit for rapamycin-era work.
